guideposts.label: 2 new stage towns on the map La Vuelta
guideposts.detail: Puçol and Xeraco make their debut as La Vuelta stage town. The full list of new stage towns in this edition: Monaco (stage 1), Manosque (2), Font-Romeu (stage 3), Falset (5), Roquetes (5), Vall d’Alba (7), Puçol (8), Xeraco (8), La Vila Joiosa (9), Alcaraz (10), Elche de la Sierra (10), Vera (12), Almuñécar (13), Palma del Rio (15), Cortegana (16), La Rábida (16), Dos Hermanas (17), El Puerto de S

guideposts.label: On the roads of the Volta a la Comunitat Valenciana
guideposts.detail: Both Puçol and Xeraco have been stage towns for the Volta a la Comunitat Valenciana, the main local cycling event in the area. The race was born as the Vuelta al Levante in 1929. The winner’s list was opened by local hero Salvador Cardona, crowned in Valencia a few weeks after he had became the first Spanish stage winner at the Tour de France. Remco Evenepoel won the 77th edition in February 2026.

guideposts.label: Pogacar’s 250th Grand Tour distinctive jersey
guideposts.detail: Tadej Pogacar received yesterday his 249th and 250th Grand Tour distinctive jerseys: - 97 as the overall leader (71 in the Tour, 6 in La Vuelta, 20 in the Giro) - 8 as the leader of points standings (3 in the Tour, 5 in La Vuelta) - 63 as the leader of the mountains standings (39 in the Tour, 4 in La Vuelta, 20 in the Giro) - 82 as the leader of the young riders standings (75 in the Tour, 7 in La

guideposts.label: Let’s roll
guideposts.detail: The peloton make their way to the start proper with an 8 km parade. There are 177 riders as Luca Van Boven (Lotto Intermarché) doesn't start after his crash yesterday.

guideposts.label: La Roja
guideposts.detail: Tadej Pogacar (UAE Emirates XRG) slightly increased his GC lead with a late attack to Aramon Valdelinares. Enric Mas (Movistar) now trails by 3’50’’, and Primoz Roglic (Red Bull-Bora-Hansgrohe) by 4’50’’. The gap to Felix Gall (Decathlon CMA CGM) is up to 5’01’’. Sepp Kuss (Visma-Lease a Bike) completes the top 5 with a gap of 6’05’’, just ahead of Oscar Onley (Netcompany Ineos), trailing by 6’06’

guideposts.label: Team standings
guideposts.detail: With Léo Bisiaux (9th), Felix Gall (20th) and Gregor Mühlberger (25th), Decathlon CMA CGM had the best collective performance again. They now lead the team standings with a gap of 12’04’’ on UAE Emirates XRG and 20’35’’ on Visma-Lease a Bike.

guideposts.label: The start is delayed
guideposts.detail: Several riders crashed as the race direction was waiting for a straggler to return to the bunch after a mechanical.

guideposts.label: Big crash in the early moments of the stage
Sinuhé Fernandez attacks as the soon the flag drops
guideposts.detail: Meanwhile, Sander De Pestel calls for the race doctor.

guideposts.label: Fernandez is 35'' ahead
guideposts.detail: His Burgos Burpellet BH teammate José Luis Faura tried tojoin him but he's been reeled in by the bunch.

guideposts.label: The gap increases to 2'20''
guideposts.detail: The race is at km 15.

guideposts.label: Ivan Sosa abandons
guideposts.detail: Kern Pharma's Colombian climber appears to have been caught in the crash before the start.

guideposts.label: Correction - Diego Uriarte is the Kern Pharma rider who abandoned
guideposts.detail: The Spaniard suffers from a ribs injury, his team reports. Ivan Sosa is still in the race.

guideposts.label: Van Tricht also abandons
guideposts.detail: Floris Van Tricht (NSN) was making his Grand Tour debut at La Vuelta 26.

guideposts.label: Fernandez is in Betera
guideposts.detail: Several stages of the Volta a la Comunitat Valenciana and the last two editions of the the Volta CV Feminas started in Betera (km 32.8). It was notably the case in 2026. Raul Garcia Pierna won the final stage of the men’s event while Remco Evenepoel sealed the overall victory; Liane Lippert won the women’s event. Betera is also the hometown of Francisco Navarro, the winner of stage 5 of La Vuelta

guideposts.label: Visma-Lease a Bike control the gap
guideposts.detail: The peloton trailed by: - 5'50'' as they passed km 24 - 5'48'' at km 27 - 5'30'' at km 30 - 5'30'' at km 32.

guideposts.label: Fernandez in his favourite role
guideposts.detail: Sinuhé Fernandez (Burgos Burpellet BH) was already part of the breakaway on the second stage, on the way to Manosque. He’s Burgos Burpellet BH’s breakaway specialist. This year, he’s attacked in two stages of O Gran Camiño, one in Itzulia and one in the GP Miguel Indurain. Last year, when he made his La Vuelta debut before having to abandon on stage 12 due to the illness that affected the team, he

guideposts.label: Winning streaks - Uno-X Mobility leads the way alongside UAE Emirates XRG and Visma-Lease a Bike
guideposts.detail: The three teams with stage wins at La Vuelta so far - UAE Emirates XRG, Visma-Lease a Bike and Uno-X Mobility - also won in the Giro d’Italia and in the Tour de France. The Norwegian team have won a stage in each of the last four Grand Tours they’ve participated in (Tour 2025, Giro 2026, Tour 2026, La Vuelta 26). For UAE Emirates XRG, the streak has been going since Tadej Pogacar’s victories at La

guideposts.label: Mattia Gaffuri abandons
guideposts.detail: Picnic PostNL's former Gran Fondo world champion was making his Grand Tour debut.

guideposts.label: Fernandez covered 43.3 km in the first hour
guideposts.detail: The peloton trail by 5'05''.

guideposts.label: Elosegui: "It brings back some very fond memories for our family"
guideposts.detail: Íñigo Elosegui (Kern Pharma) had great stories to tell this morning at the start: “Yes, my grandfather [José Antonio Momeñe] won in Valencia in 1966. And on top of that, he took the lead in La Vuelta! It brings back some very fond memories for our family. I’ve also won a few races here in the Valencian Community, so it’s a place that brings back fond memories for us. I’ve always wanted to follow i

guideposts.label: 4 minutes
guideposts.detail: Sinuhé Fernandez (Burgos Burpellet BH) is 104 km from the finish, and the peloton are 4'05'' behind him.

guideposts.label: 100 kilometres to go
guideposts.detail: The gap keeps decreasing steadily: 3'55''.

guideposts.label: The average speed after 2 hours: 41.9 km/h
guideposts.detail: Sinuhé Fernandez (Burgos-Burpellet-BH) is 75 km from the finish. The peloton trail by 2'25''.

guideposts.label: The gap decreases again: 1'40''
guideposts.detail: Sinuhé Fernandez (Burgos Burpellet BH) is 65 km from the finish.

guideposts.label: Headed for the intermediate sprint and the Puerto de Barx
guideposts.detail: Puerto de Barx is an emblematic ascent in the area, very often featured in the Volta a la Comunitat Valenciana. Both in 2025 and 2026, it has been the perfect launchpad for Demi Vollering to take her first victory of the season in Gandia, right next to Xeraco.

guideposts.label: Fernandez is caught at km 133
guideposts.detail: Meanwhile, there was a crash in the peloton involving Ethan Hayter (Soudal Quick-Step) and Lars Craps (Lotto Intermarché). They both rapidly got backon their feet.

guideposts.label: The average speed after 3 hours: 41.0 km/h
guideposts.detail: The peloton significantly accelerate ahead of the intermediate sprint and the climb.

guideposts.label: Pogacar caught in a crash
guideposts.detail: The Slovenian gets back up but it was a hard tumble. He's suffering from his left arm.

guideposts.label: Tadej Pogacar abandons La Vuelta 26
guideposts.detail: The Slovenian leader of the race walked to the ambulance.

guideposts.label: 25 kilometres to the finish
guideposts.detail: The peloton went over the top at a moderate pace. Now Xabier Mikel Azparren (Pinarello Q36.5) attacks. Visma-Lease a Bike drive the peloton.

guideposts.label: Tadej Pogacar is forced to abandon La Vuelta
Pogacar had never abandoned a stage race
guideposts.detail: This is his first withdrawal since Liège-Bastogne-Liège in 2023. He is the first overall leader of La Vuelta to crash out of the race since Igor Anton in 2010 (stage 14).

guideposts.label: 10 kilometres to go
guideposts.detail: Azparren is still 14 seconds ahead. There's been another crash in the peloton.

guideposts.label: Carlos Rodriguez caught in the crash
guideposts.detail: The Spaniard rapidly resumed racing. Roland Thalmann is the last rider to get back on his bike, with his jersey completely torn.

guideposts.label: 2 seconds with 2 km to go
guideposts.detail: Azparren is about to be caught.

guideposts.label: Azparren is caught 1.5 km from the line
guideposts.detail: Netcompany Ineos are at the front.

guideposts.label: Bryan Coquard wins stage 8 of La Vuelta 26!
guideposts.detail: There was another mass crash in the final kilometre.

guideposts.label: Top 5
guideposts.detail: 1. Bryan Coquard (Cofidis) 2. Mads Pedersen (Lidl-Trek) 3. Jordi Meeus (Red Bull-Bora-Hansgrohe) 4. Ben Turner (Netcompany Ineos) 5. Jordan Labrosse (Decathlon CMA CGM)

guideposts.label: Enric Mas is the new overall leader of La Vuelta 26
guideposts.detail: He becomes the first Spanish leader of La Vuelta since Jesus Herrada in 2018.
